title: Notes of Ministry - 55 - June 1977

source.file: Various/Notes of Ministry - 55 - June 1977 (2436)/Notes of Ministry - 55 - June 1 - Various.epub

paragraphs.text: My desire, dear brethren, is to say something about pleasing God. Naturally we please ourselves, particularly when we are younger. “When thou wast young”, the Lord said to Peter, “thou girdedst thyself, and walkedst where thou desiredst; but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and bring thee where thou dost not desire”, John 21: 18. When we are young we are often ambitious, we want to go where we will. But the Lord Jesus, I believe, would exercise our hearts that there might be a greater concern with us to please God, rather than to please ourselves. “For the Christ also did not please himself” (Romans 15: 3); we might have thought He was entitled to do so, being who He was. But it says. He “did not please himself; but according as it is written, The reproaches of them that reproach thee have fallen upon me”. I suppose that was because He was always pleasing to His Father.

I refer then first of all to this passage in Luke because there is to Him the expression of the Father’s pleasure, or delight, in Him, absolutely and infinitely perfect. There had been others before Him, such as David, who is referred to by God as “a man after my heart” (Acts 13: 22), but David failed, as we know, and he failed very badly too. Nevertheless in character, as typical of

Jesus, he was a man after God’s heart. But when we come to Jesus we come to a Person the like of whom there never was before, nor has there ever been since in blood and flesh, and the Father signalises this by a voice out of heaven, “Thou art my beloved Son, in thee I have found my delight”. We have often been reminded that that would refer to the thirty years of His life hidden and secret. There was nothing within that was ever against the Father, no wrong motives or impulses, no sin. He was begotten, as we know, of the Holy Spirit; the conception was by the power of the Spirit, and He was as Man in flesh and blood free from any taint of sin whatever. There was no other man like Him.

We might refer back to Isaac’s birth, which in a certain sense was miraculous, but he was of Abraham and Sarah. But Jesus was unique. He was Himself, and the only One in whom there was no taint of sin whatever. Hence the Father says, ‘ In Thee I have found My delight’. He is not referring, as far as I understand it, to what He did, although the Father’s pleasure would surely be in that, but to what He, the “knower of the hearts of all” (Acts 1: 24), found in Him.

The purity of motive, the affections towards His Father, His perfection in dependence and subjection as Man, all flowed from what He was within. If we think of the burnt-offering we find that the inwards and the legs are referred to, but there is no reference to the kidneys.

There was no need for purification with Jesus at all, and His walk was the perfect expression of what He was within. Hence He was the only One upon whom the Holy Spirit could descend as a dove and find a resting place with nothing out of accord with His holy nature, and nothing out of accord with the Father.

So Jesus, first of all, is spoken to—“Thou art …”. What that must have meant to the Father, to have a Man after so many years, four thousand plus, perhaps, in whom He had found His delight! What it must have meant to Jesus for the Father to say that to Him. I would love to have some sense of approval from God, but none in blood and flesh could ever have that unqualified approval from the Father save Jesus. So we find Him alone, but He takes His place in lowliness with the people and is “baptised and praying”. I think, dear brethren, we can take our model from Him and be marked more by identification with the people. I think you will find with all those who have served the saints in such a distinguished way in the recovery that they have always taken the saints where they have found them and, associating themselves with them, have served them so that they might be in practice what they are in the divine view. Now, Jesus here was baptised. As to Himself, He needed it not. No doubt there is an implied figure of His own death, so essential if any were to come into blessing, and the Father would find His delight in that, but what I would like to emphasize is that the Father found Him inwardly, in His every motive, thought, and affection, absolutely in accord with Himself.

When the Holy Spirit descended in Acts 2 as “parted tongues, as of fire”, it sat upon each one of them. The root of sin was in them, and the root of sin is in every man and woman until he or she dies. Let us not be carried away with any doctrine of sinless perfection. It is not the truth; it is against the truth; let us not presume it. There was only one Man in blood and flesh in whom the root of sin did not exist and that was Jesus. So the fire sat upon them; it was essential for the negating of the evil that was there in

the flesh I have no doubt. Many came into the good of that, and the exercise is for us to do the same, but what I call attention to in the contrast is this, that the Holy Spirit descended upon Jesus as a dove and found a resting place upon and in One who was in perfect accord with Him.
Now in John 8 the Lord Jesus refers to Himself. We have all heard of ‘the Man of John 8’.

We often speak of ‘the man of John 9’ and, of course, we do well to do so because he is a wonderful example of “the works of God”, John 9: 3. But when we contemplate the Man Jesus of John 8 we find that He is in conflict there. He can say of Himself, “Altogether that which I also say to you”, John 8: 25. His speech was the expression of Himself. Often, I find with myself, and perhaps you do too, that what I say is not truly a reflection of what is passing through my mind, in fact, it could be the opposite; but with Jesus what He said was the perfect expression of Himself, with no trace of hypocrisy, or of anything inconsistent. As I think of the ark (Exodus 25: 11) it was the same without as it was within, and no one could look into it. What would be the point in any case? There was the outward, the same as the inward, and I think of the Lord Jesus like that, “Altogether that which I also say to you”.

‘Who do you make yourself?’, they say to Him. Think of their saying that to Jesus! “Whom makest thou thyself? “(John 8: 53). It has often occurred to me when thinking of their gibe at Jesus that He “made himself of no reputation” (A.V.). He “emptied himself”, Philippians 2: 7.

Think of this lowly Man here in conflict, the perfect expression in His speech of what He was inwardly. Hence He says to them, “He that has sent me … has not left me alone”; now notice the word, ‘because I do always the things that are pleasing to

Him’. What things were those? I suppose we could go through the gospels and see them. He was very limited in the area in which He lived. I do not know how many miles Jesus travelled, or what area He covered; it was not as many miles as some of us have travelled. He was very limited in His circumstances, a poor Man, and yet doing always those things that pleased the Father. Therefore the Father did not leave Him alone. The Father was with Him in that bitter conflict. Think of the persons who opposed Him—the religious hierarchy, and the Jews, and Jesus in the presence of it maintaining the truth as a Man, “a man who has spoken the truth to you” (John 8: 40). They claim Abraham as their father. They go back to the origin. Sometimes we may be inclined to do that. Some claim that they are the continuation of the recovery. God does not look at things like that. The question is what I am morally under His eye as He takes account of me. The Jews make this claim to Abraham in the presence of Jesus. They say, “We are not born of fornication” (John 8: 41). They claim a genealogy without mixture whilst accusing Him of being a Samaritan (John 8: 48). But in the midst of the conflict He was never left alone by the Father “because I do always the things that are pleasing to him”. Well, that is the Lord Jesus, about whom I feel I have spoken very feebly.

Now we come to John’s reference to ourselves, “Beloved, if our heart condemn us not, we have boldness towards God, and whatsoever we ask we receive from him, because we keep his commandments, and practise the things which are pleasing in his sight”. “If our heart condemn us not”—you can see, in the principle of it, a certain similarity to the Lord’s words, although leaving the Lord unique. Can that apply to all? Can that apply to our young people?
You may think immediately,

when you speak of practising the things that are pleasing in His sight, of great exploits. You might think of being a distinguished preacher, or someone who has some prominent place in the testimony. I doubt if that is really what is in mind, although it may be included. I think practising the things that are pleasing in His sight would involve simple righteousness. If, for example, I am due to start at nine o’clock at the office, I should be there at nine o’clock, not five minutes late! If I am due to leave at five, I leave at five, not five minutes to—all these simple things in life. I maintain my simple relations with my wife, with my children, with the brethren. I maintain what is right in the assembly. I come into the assembly in a dignified way. If I came into the room and there was nobody in it, I might not take my hat off. That would not matter. If I felt so disposed I might whistle a little, or sing; but if I came in and there were one or two members of the assembly sitting there I would immediately recognise the assembly and act accordingly.

All these simple practices in life, dear brethren, are included in “the things which are pleasing in his sight”. Not just that you avoid the things that are displeasing; John does not put it like that. There is no doubt, of course, that you would; but the exercise is positively to “practise the things which are pleasing in his sight”. And we “keep his commandments”; in point of fact he puts that first, “We keep his commandments, and practise the things which are pleasing in his sight “. Now I think the Lord Jesus would exercise us about this so that our relationships are maintained rightly here under the eye of God. And remember this, please, that with God it is never ‘out of sight, out of mind’, never! We are always in His sight; no matter where we are His eye is upon us. “The

eyes of Jehovah are in every place, beholding the evil and the good”, Proverbs 15: 3. We are never out of God’s sight. Sometimes we are out of the sight of our brethren; in fact we are out of their sight more than we are in it, but with God it is never ‘out of sight, out of mind’; we are always in His view. Let us be exercised to “practise the things which are pleasing in his sight”.

Then consider the reference to keeping His commandments; “And this is his commandment, that we believe on the name of his Son Jesus Christ, and that we love one another, even as he has given us commandment”. What a commandment that was! “A new commandment I give to you, that ye love one another … By this shall all know that ye are disciples of mine, if ye have love amongst yourselves”, John 13: 34, 35. I find that I link all kinds of things with discipleship which the Lord does not link with discipleship at all. This is how men will know
“that ye are disciples of mine, if ye have love amongst yourselves”.

Now, dear brethren, I fully agree that you cannot love to order, and you cannot manufacture love. You cannot suddenly decide, ‘Well, I will love So-and-so’, can you? That is not possible. How then can we come into this affection for one another? How can we have love
‘amongst ourselves’? Someone once said, ‘Well, if you see love is missing, bring it in!’. If you see sympathy is missing, bring it in. Do not be critical because it is not there; bring it in!

If you go into a brother’s house and some necessity is not there, do not criticize him because it is not there—give him what is needed. That is it; bring in what is needed! And so it is in the assembly—bring it in. But, I believe, beloved brethren, the way in which we can be maintained in love for one another

is by strengthening our link with Christ. The more we strengthen our link with Christ by seeking His presence, seeking His face, looking into His word, the more our love for Him will develop and the more, necessarily, will our love for one another develop too. That is the way, I think, that love is brought about. It is not a mental decision, not a conscious decision to form love or try to love, but the more we are with God, the more we shall be formed according to His nature and the more we shall love one another.

My final passage, in 1 Thessalonians 4, refers to walking ‘so as to please’ God (see footnote to verse 1). The apostle here commands the Thessalonians. He says, “We … exhort you in the Lord Jesus, even as ye have received from us how ye ought to walk and please God, even as ye also do walk, that ye would abound still more”. “Still more”; there is always room for further abounding, so as to walk and please God, that is, in our passage through the world.

Perhaps I could remind you of what is very well known, that these were young believers, young in the faith, and Paul speaks to them of serious things a little later, about which young people need to be warned. In this so-called ‘permissive society’ sin is regarded lightly, and I find men are not only completely disregarding the institutions of God, such as marriage, but they have no thought whatever of walking in righteousness. Another thing I have noticed is that the word sin is dropping out of the general conversation of men. They use all kinds of terms to cover up sin. Now Paul is warning these young believers to walk so as to please God. Do not allow this ‘permissive society’ to affect you. Keep near to God. If your links with God and with the Lord Jesus are not maintained,

then the environment of the world will affect you. And we all know full well that what we have been taught is true, that what exists in any city is likely, if there is not care, to infiltrate into the assembly. Now, young people, I would like to exhort you to take care in this
‘permissive society’ and be exercised to walk so as to please God. I would say in simplicity and faith, “even as ye also do”, but “abound still more”.

And what is the conclusion of the chapter? We “shall be caught up … to meet the Lord in the air”. I have often in my mind written ‘Enoch’ across this chapter. He walked so as to please God; “Before his translation he has the testimony that he had pleased God”; he “was not found, because God had translated him”, Hebrews 11: 5. That would be similar to ourselves, walking so as to please God, and we shall not be, because God will take us! I understand that Mr. Darby said towards the end of his life, ‘Well, now I am going to be taken; the question is, What will the Lord say to me?’. You have to keep Scripture in its context. The rapture is based on grace, therefore every believer will be there. We can well be continually reminded of that. But then there is the judgment seat, and what will He say to me there? Everything will be assessed perfectly. He will approve nothing that should be disapproved. He could not possibly say that anything that was right was wrong. What will He say to me? Now that is 75

brought home to us in our present responsibility so that our consciences and hearts might be exercised, so that we might walk so as to please God, and when raptured what God raptures is a people that please Him. So, as we have been reminded, may we be reminded again, that the assembly is not transferred to heaven because she failed on earth; she is transferred to heaven because she belongs there,
and I believe there will be few when the Lord takes the saints away, those here, if but a few, who are walking so as to please Him. May every one of us here be in that company, for His pleasure.
It would be very good for every one of us to possess the peace which is spoken of is these scriptures. The Lord, coming into the midst of His own said, “Peace be to you”, John 20: 19.

That was a very elevated level of peace. We will all have noticed that He said it twice; and after the second time “he breathed into them, and says to them, Receive the Holy Spirit”, as if such persons were to be characterised by that and able to move here in the power of the Holy Spirit, thus resenting Him. I think this is one of the highest things that the gospel contemplates for men—that they should be representing Jesus, and also, as it says in Ephesians, be imitators of God. To be able for this we have to be regulated by the peace of God.

In our time we see man going on without joy, without peace; but the gospel, becoming effective in us, does not leave us without joy and peace. As the word of God goes out to man; he is to obey it. That is a necessity. The most dreadful thing for a man is the rejection of the word of God,

the glad tidings, in treating it indifferently. Oh, what it must mean to God, man despising these glad tidings, the glad tidings of Jesus who in such obedience went this way, to bring about repentance with sinners and to save them.
There are only two classes of men, and everybody belongs to one class. He cannot be in both.

Romans makes this clear for us. The word here tells us in an absolute way—“For as indeed by the disobedience of the one man the many have been constituted sinners”. That is one class of men; but then there is that which came in by Christ “so also by the obedience of the one the many will be constituted righteous”. What a blessed difference—that such sinners can become pardoned sinners.

In one sense it remains with us, as Paul says, “… sinners, of whom I am the first”, 1 Timothy 1: 15. But that is no longer the class of sinners who do not receive the word of God, but pardoned sinners, who have forgiveness by faith in the blood of Jesus. That is what God is offering in the glad tidings. One might say that it is the plainest thing on earth, yet often it is the most difficult. Why is that so? Because it exposes clearly whether one is prepared to be subject, or not. If we do not surrender, then we are on very dangerous ground but what blessedness to be subject to Him who thus becomes Lord to us.

It is of all importance that “by the obedience of the one the many will be constituted righteous”, for without this foundation it is impossible for us to have peace. The first verse of this chapter, says, “Therefore having been justified on the principle of faith, we have peace towards God”. This is an essential matter, to have peace towards God, and it comes by being justified. It is the
longing of us all—the longing also of divine Persons—that you might have peace towards God, that your sins should no longer be between you and God. For sins can be forgiven—

how great God is “Their sins and their lawlessnesses I will never remember any more”, Hebrews 10: 17. We see the aboundings of grace, as it says, “but where sin abounded, grace has overabounded”, Romans 5: 20. What overaboundings of the grace of God, providing the means by which any may have peace towards God. Oh what it means to be subject to Him who went into death for me and for you, who shed His precious blood that your and my sins might be forgiven. What a Saviour He is—and we have to do, with Him. Every man will have to do with Him. Dreadful it will be for a man to, have to do with Him as Judge! But, how wonderful, He is now the Saviour of sinners.

Then we have to understand, our sins being forgiven, that we need to be led further to understand that not only were our sins atoned for, but that the whole man who sinned has gone at the cross. I believe that an understanding of this helps us to enjoy the peace of God.

The first thing is forgiveness, justification, and peace towards God. But I believe the peace of God is something further, as understanding that the man of sin and shame has been put away, as Paul says, “No longer live, I, but Christ lives in me”, Galatians 2: 20. What a day that is for us to reach, so that we go on in peace, enjoying the peace of God.

So it says in Romans 8 that the law has no more claim upon us, “there is then now no condemnation, to those in Christ Jesus. For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set me free from the law of sin and of death”. It is a wonderful thing to live in afresh atmosphere, no longer under bondage. I believe many of us know something of that. Bondage

comes in when man has the sceptre in his hand; then there is no peace. I believe that many, though having peace towards God—are still athirst after this peace, longing to enjoy the peace of God, no longer to be under bondage; but in liberty, as it says, “the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus”—to enjoy life. That is our portion, beloved brethren, not a poor portion but, as we were recently reminded, “good measure, pressed down, and shaken together”, Luke 6: 38. Such is God’s giving, and to get the gain of it we need to avail ourselves of the power of the Holy Spirit. He is our nearest Friend on earth, here to form us, 77

to lead us, and to bring us into the things of God. How do we regard Him? What intercourse do we have with Him? What are our relations with the Holy Spirit? These things have had an essential part in the recovery of the truth. Let us go in fully for these things. Let us seize our full portion! If the children of Israel had fully entered into their inheritance what an inheritance God would have had in His people. So when the saints are possessing their inheritance, what an inheritance God has!

I think it is something wonderful to see persons going on in this peace. It means that we are to be regulated by the Holy Spirit. So what comes out in this eighth chapter is that persons, even in the wilderness; are led by the Spirit, “as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are sons of God (Romans 8: 14)—a wonderful thing, even in wilderness surroundings to be led in this peace, and to be in the gain of it. When others are without peace and without joy, can I be in peace and joy? If that is not the case, then we can pursue after it, we can arrive at it, as it says, “For the mind of the flesh is death; but the mind of the Spirit life and peace”. What a glorious atmosphere! Yet there

is this serious warning as to “the mind of the flesh”. Who could say that he is always free of it? But what gain is there in it? A merchant is always seeking gain, and in a spiritual way we should be merchants, those who can trade with the talent. That involves our responsibility, as related to the Spirit. Am I subject to the Spirit? It says, “The mind of the Spirit life and peace”. Is my mind in accord with the mind of the Spirit? In 1 Corinthians 12: 13 it says, “In the power of one Spirit we have all been baptised into one body … and have all been given to drink of one Spirit”. We are lifted up into the sphere of the Spirit. In the power of these things we are able to move on in accord with the mind of the Spirit and thus we shall prove life and peace. What it means to God to have persons going on in the power of life, in joy and happiness, and in the peace of God. What a result can then be reached in the service of God.

In Philippians 4 Paul is showing the way to normal christianity. Man normally is not thankful. In searching ourselves we know how much we may be still marked by that. How often I find myself not being thankful. Yet one who has the forgiveness of sins, and who knows that the old man has been completely set aside at the cross and in the death of Christ, should be marked by thankfulness, in the sense that God has cleared such a way to His heart in blessedness.

Paul says, “Be careful about nothing; but in everything, by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God”. It is a matter of dependence; I must be moving in dependence in the power of the Spirit to do this. With thanksgiving, by prayer and supplication, we bring our requests. What are our requests? If we care for the things of God, then we will have a

wide outlook in a spiritual way in relation to our requests. They will reach out further than our personal matters. How necessary our personal matters are, and we should be going on in power and joy, but there is more than that—there is the universal position; we know that difficulties arise, but we are able to move on in peace in spite of things around us.
Paul says in Colossians 3: 15, “Let the peace of Christ preside in your hearts”, meaning that every decision of our hearts is regulated by the peace of Christ. Is that really the case with us?

I think that, as we arrive at it, we shall find it a wonderful matter. So our scripture says, “The peace of God … shall guard your hearts and your thoughts by Christ Jesus”. If the gospel effects that with every one of us, then we shall be available to take on more of the character of this glorious Person who has effectuated everything for us, so as to give testimony to Him.

We all know how essential testimony is, beloved brethren. Things have been made known to us, testified to us, exemplified to us by persons who have lived in these things. What gain have we had from them? I think we can all get the greatest gain as we desire to be such persons as Paul is presenting to the Philippians—those walking in the peace of God which surpasses every understanding, as preserved by Christ Jesus. What an elevated pathway!—
how triumphant, over against those who mind earthly things, as it says in this epistle, who are

“the enemies of the cross of Christ”, Philippians 3: 18. Such are not regulated by peace; they mind the things of the flesh, what gratifies themselves. The test would be, can I be subject to the Spirit, whom God has given on account of Christ being glorified, and thus go on in dependence, in the peace of God, which surpasses every understanding? May it be increasingly so, for His name’s sake.

articles.title: WHAT MUST I DO TO BE SAVED?
articles.author: D. Robertson

paragraphs.text: The gospel is like no other word that is spoken in the world because it comes from God. It brings us into the presence of divine speaking, and the fact that God is speaking is a very solemn thing. Hebrews 12: 25, speaking about persons who disregarded the speaking of Moses, a man, and of the punishment meted out to them, says, “See that ye refuse not him that speaks. For if those did not escape who had refused him who uttered the oracles on earth, much more we who turn away from him who does so from heaven”. That is what the gospel is; it is speaking from heaven. There is nothing more important than to hear and to answer the speaking from heaven. I would just like to say that as you are under the sound of the gospel tonight you have to do with God. You cannot escape having to do with God. If you refuse to have to do with God it will be to your eternal loss. There will be many who find themselves in the lake of fire eternally, the punishment of those who refuse the speaking of Him who speaks from heaven.

It will be a terrible thing for persons who find themselves there, who have refused the speaking from God, who have refused to have to do with God in a time of grace. I would appeal specially to the young people here that they might have to do with God. It is not a hard thing. It is a delightful and happy thing in the day of grace to have to do with God. But it will be a terrible thing to have to do with God if you refuse the Lord Jesus and refuse divine speaking. It says, “What shall be the end of those who obey not the glad tidings of God?”, 1 Peter 4: 17.

Have you ever stopped and thought a little and perhaps wondered whether God is saying that to you? Just stop and think about it. God would be very homely, friendly, and affectionate in the way He would speak to us. He might be saying, if you stopped and thought, ‘What is going to be your end if you continue to refuse to answer to the voice of Him who speaks from heaven?’. You remember a man called Pilate before whom the Lord Jesus was brought to be judged. In the middle of the judgment his wife came to him because God had spoken to her.

She had a message for him from God. This was the message—“Have thou nothing to do with that righteous man”, Matthew 27: 19. The whole mob was branding Him as unrighteous, yet God in His grace secured testimony in the heart of this woman that He was a righteous man.
I have no doubt in my mind that Pilate will be present at the great white throne. He tried to wash his hands of the whole thing, as if he were innocent, but he was just as guilty as the rest.

I believe God will say in infinite fairness to Pilate, ‘Do you remember the word that I sent through your wife to you? Why did you not accept it?’. That will be the position of everyone who refuses Him who speaks from heaven. Is that going to be your position? There is no need for anyone in this room ever to be before the great white throne. You can come before the throne of God now and find, not judgment, but grace—you can find a Saviour.
Here in Acts 16 is a man who is brought before the throne of grace. His reaction is a right—

reaction. He is not seeking to escape the voice from heaven. Oh it was a voice from heaven, through Paul, from the innermost prison cells; more than that, it reached into the innermost parts of this hard jailor’s heart. There is nothing like the mercy of God to break down your heart. God can get in where man could never get in. You may have hidden from Him for years, but there comes the time when, in His grace, God reaches into your heart. He names you. ‘I want you’. He says; ‘It is time you listened to Me and gave Me your heart, gave Me your ear. I want to speak to you about your eternal blessing. I want to tell you I have a Saviour for you who can save you for time and for eternity’. Praise be to His glorious name!

Does everyone here know that Saviour? If you do not, thank God the door is wide open for you tonight. Go in, and God would speak from heaven in love to your soul. He spoke in love to this man’s soul, a man who had been marked not by love but by hatred. He had beaten the servants of God and fastened them securely in the inner prison. Ah! that does not deter God from seeking this man’s blessing. What a God He is! undeterred by refusal, rejection, and man’s attitude towards Him, his callousness and even hatred. God still seeks man’s blessing.

Oh what a God, what a Saviour God, we announce! Friend, are you going to listen to God tonight? Let God’s word, let God Himself, arrest you. In God’s grace let the light shine into your soul. What will the light do? At first divine light does not make you happy. It awakens you to the fact that you have a need and that you are a sinner. Divine light exposes you at first and you say, ‘Yes, I am a sinner, and more than that, a sinner in the sight of God’. That is the point
this man came to. “What must I do that I may be saved?”. Oh friend, come to it tonight,
‘What must I do?’. It is not a question of your father or mother; their faith is of no avail to you. You must believe and be convicted for yourself.

God in His grace would work with you and look into your heart, that you might be brought to the point, the simple, blessed point that this man was brought to, so that you say, ‘What must I do to be saved?’. Does anyone know the answer? Certainly we know; we who are believers know the answer, and we would surround you and make it easy for you. We would tell you,

“Believe on the Lord Jesus and thou shalt be saved”. O, friend, it is a joyous thing to tell you, because it is the way we have all come. Thank God we can covet to walk in the light! Do not miss the opportunity! You may never have another one. Pilate never had another. It is as sure as I am here tonight that Pilate is in a lost eternity and that he will appear before God in that final day at the great white throne. There will not be a word he can say. Every mouth will be stopped (see Romans 3: 19).

We appeal to you to let the Lord Jesus into your heart. We can speak, and our speaking may be feeble at the best, but what we are relying on is that God will act in your soul tonight and bring you to this point. He would tell you that not only do you have a need, but that there is only one Person who can meet your need. He has been to the cross. He has taken on the question of sin and sins, and as far as God is concerned He has discharged the whole thing before God. He suffered to that end. No one suffered like Jesus. Those nails would not have held Jesus on the cross if He had not wanted to stay there. What held Him there? It was His love, first of all for God, so that the

name of God might be glorified in relation to every challenge of evil, and then for the sinner, that he might know salvation. How we love to sing of ‘Salvation’s sweet story’. I feel my heart is singing because it is in there, for “of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks”, Matthew 12: 34.
I tell you in simplicity, the way is wide open for you. Acts 14: 27 speaks of God having

“opened a door of faith to the nations”. That is the way we have been blessed. God has done it. Thanks be to our Saviour God! Whoever has been blessed, it is God who has done it. Do not miss the present opportunity. You need a Saviour, and thank God there is a divinely provided Saviour. We would say in all affection—we would join with God in appealing to you—“Believe on the Lord Jesus and thou shalt be saved”.

It may be you are saved and have already the light in your soul that you owe your eternal salvation to Jesus. Now how are you living? In Exodus 2 we read of persons who were in a similar position to many believers today. Jesus has met them and He helped them when they were in a helpless position and could not help themselves. That is the experience of those who could not help themselves but have had their sins forgiven through the name of Jesus and who thus know the blessedness of salvation. The question is, ‘Where is He?’. He was here with a few of us this morning. What did we do? Did we leave Him out of our reckoning?

Were we doing something independently of Jesus? He said, “This do in remembrance of me”, 1 Corinthians 11: 24. Where is He in relation to you, young friend? You owe your eternal salvation to Him. He is the One who has died to secure salvation for you and has brought the knowledge of forgiveness to your soul. You owe everything to Him. Where is He? “Why then have ye
left the man behind?”. That is the question. Why did you not take up your blessing? Well, there is some barrier. Ah, cast the barrier down! The Spirit of God is on your side tonight.

The mighty power of the grace of God is all in your favour that you might not leave Christ behind. Give Him the place He deserves, and do it tonight crown Him Lord of all. I want to leave this question with you, ‘Where is the Man?’. Did you remember Him? Are you reckoning with Him? Is He in every department of your life? If not, why not? Remember, you owe your eternal salvation to Him.

These are simple, real, blessed questions that God would put to you, not to put you in a tight corner, or to embarrass you; but that you may answer to the blessed Son of His love. May you do so! Do not leave the Man behind any longer. You have left Him behind long enough; answer to His call. There are certain desires of His that He wants you to fill out. He wants you to be a testimony in the short while left to us. I think that these questions are addressed to us all. Where is He? This Man who helped you, saved you, and to whom you owe the forgiveness of your sins; this Man who has made eternity secure for you, where is He? “Why then have ye left the man behind?”. May the divine appeal of love find an answer in your heart!

The Lord Jesus has a very special love for you and He expects you to answer to it. It is a blessed thing to have part with saints, those who have been blessed through the redeeming blood of Christ, and who are moved in their affections so that they seek for the rest of their time to be faithful to His love. That is just the setting in which this man raised the question,
“Why then have ye left the man behind?”. Do not leave Him behind any longer. He makes His appeal in His own gracious
way, and we would appeal to you not to ignore it but to answer to it, for His name’s sake!

articles.title: CHRIST AS THE CENTRE OF ATTRACTION
articles.author: D. R. Freeman

paragraphs.text: John the baptist’s testimony (John 1: 29–37) indicates Christ as the centre of attraction for God and for men. As Man here, the Spirit was drawn forth upon Him (John 1: 32), committed in the fullest way as “descending and abiding”. For men He must be the centre of attraction because of who He is John says “He was before me”—but also because of His suffering character as the Lamb, the One who was lifted up. John speaks of Him not only as the Son of God (John 1: 34), a divine Person, but also as the Lamb, God’s Lamb, showing that he understood the necessity for His death. It was this latter in his exclamation, “Behold the Lamb of God”, which affected his two disciples so that they followed Jesus. The walk of Jesus—for he sees Jesus as He walked—was attractive both to heaven and to men, having in view, but by way of the cross, the securing of conditions of rest both for God and for men. So the two disciples “abode with him that day”, thus anticipating the end of all the work and toil on account of which He came.
Kingston, Ont.

articles.title: “COME, LORD JESUS”
articles.author: Q. Poore
articles.place: His love for ever with Thee shared.

paragraphs.text: Lord Jesus, come, it is Thy right;
Come in Thy glory, love, and might
To take Thine own, then we shall be
Content for ever Lord, with Thee.
How long, Lord Jesus, till Thou’lt come—
To see Thy face Thy people long—
Thou who hast loved us, made us free,
That Thou might’st claim us, Lord, for Thee;
Till Thou shalt come, with all Thine own,
And shine through all, on Thine own throne,
When all shall see Thy glories beam,
And Thou shalt reign, O Lord, supreme?
E’en now we love Thyself to see,
And by the Spirit near Thee be,
As those who prove His power and love,
His witness to Thyself above.
Lord Jesus, come! E’en so Lord, come
And take us to Thy Father’s home,
To that blest place Thou hast prepared,
